scope: Implementation sequence 1: installed external tooling contract; not production browser integration or annotation interaction acceptance
verified: Named headed Chromium launch through installed playwright-cli open --headed --profile=<absolute> --config=<absolute>.
JSON browser.launchOptions.executablePath and extension args load an unpacked MV3 service worker.

Existing spike annotation extension loads through the installed CLI; chrome.runtime manifest reports Cockpit Space feedback 0.1.0. The spike controller was not started and annotation submission was not tested.
The session resolves from its .playwright workspace and a nested directory.
The same session name fails from /tmp outside that workspace with an actionable browser-not-open error.
A shell started before browser launch discovers the later browser using an explicit session name, without a new browser environment variable.
tab-new about:blank returns indexed tab descriptions and preserves the original tab. Two same-URL tabs remain distinct.
A separate page-context check retained original window state while adding a tab.
Scoped close followed by explicit profile reopen reconnects and retains extension storage. The reopened browser had one tab, not restored arbitrary page memory.
Only the uniquely named owned session was closed; close-all, kill-all and delete-data were not used.

adapter_contract.launch: Run configured executable in an association-owned directory containing .playwright. Pass -s=<association-session> open [url] --headed --profile=<absolute-profile> --config=<absolute-config>.
adapter_contract.existing_url: Use scoped tab-new <url>, never open or goto on an existing session. Do not retry an uncertain URL-open outcome.
adapter_contract.agent_addressing: Include the association working directory alongside the configured executable and named session. A bare session name is insufficient from another Playwright workspace.
adapter_contract.discovery: Installed CLI registry lookup uses the nearest .playwright ancestor, bounded to ten levels. Session receipts include workspaceDir, socketPath, timestamp, embedded version and resolved profile/launch configuration. A receipt alone is not live ownership proof.
adapter_contract.tab_identity: CLI tab-list/tab-new return current numeric indices. These are transient addressing instructions, not durable document or annotation identifiers.
adapter_contract.ownership: CLI open starts a detached daemon. Cockpit must independently verify live process generation and receipt identity before scoped close or crash reconciliation. Killing the finite CLI invocation alone is not browser shutdown.
adapter_contract.supported_versions: Only CLI 0.1.5 with the recorded embedded Playwright and Chromium executable has been exercised. No broader version range is claimed.

remaining_gates: Production owner discovery, Space identity, concurrent open and shutdown integration.
Toolbar-scoped capture permissions versus controller-assisted capture, with a real live-page annotation smoke.
Durable feedback fetch/acknowledgement, local image reading, direct paste and native/browser daily-use acceptance.
